briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon, everyone. Let's begin the climate briefing for August 19, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Climate Crisis and the Need for Urgent Response
sections.content: News collected today clearly illustrates various aspects of the deepening global climate crisis. This summer, in particular, European waters reached record high temperatures, with some areas recording sea temperatures 6°C above average, which scientists analyze as a 'mass proliferation' marine heatwave caused by climate change and carbon pollution, warning of severe threats to marine life [219, 220, 221, 224, 239, 240, 243, 245]. Domestically and internationally, droughts and heavy rains are occurring simultaneously, and concerns about the deterioration of children's mental health and delayed brain development due to heatwaves, as well as the economic burden of 'heatflation,' are being raised [9, 21, 50]. Representative Kang Hoon-sik emphasized the need to enhance national disaster prevention capabilities and promptly improve related infrastructure in line with climate change [6, 11]. This indicates that the climate crisis is no longer a distant future problem but an urgent reality directly impacting our daily lives and survival.

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Domestic and International Climate Change Adaptation and Strengthening Marine Resilience
sections.content: In response to the deepening climate crisis, domestic and international efforts to enhance climate change adaptation and resilience are actively underway. Korea is contributing to the international community by utilizing marine science and technology to provide training and cooperation aimed at enhancing the climate change response capabilities and marine resilience of APEC member economies [1, 2, 3, 10, 14]. Domestically, the willingness of facility horticulture farmers to adopt technologies for climate change response is being discussed, and customized adaptation efforts in the agricultural sector are continuing, such as potato cultivation technology training in Seosan City and grape cultivation technology training in Hampyeong County [5, 7, 17, 18, 24, 31, 34, 37, 39, 41, 46, 47]. Furthermore, the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries, in collaboration with the private sector, is creating 'sea forests' in areas like Goseong, Gyeongnam, to strengthen marine ecosystem resilience in response to climate change [23, 26, 32]. Adaptation efforts in the health sector are also noteworthy, such as the establishment of a 'climate-adapted health system' in the Amazon region of South America to combat infectious diseases exacerbated by the climate crisis [8].

sections.title: 🌱 Efforts Towards a Carbon-Neutral Society
sections.content: The transition to a carbon-neutral society is leading to concrete actions, primarily driven by corporations and local governments. LG announced strengthened climate change response by publishing its '2025 ESG Report' [4, 13, 20, 27, 35, 40, 42, 49, 51], and Hana Financial Group is encouraging carbon-neutral practices in daily life through its 'HANA Green Mate' campaign, involving employees and customers [59, 60, 61, 67, 76, 78, 84, 85, 86, 87, 92, 94, 95, 101, 108, 111, 112, 115, 117, 120, 121, 123, 124, 134, 135, 140, 144, 145, 147, 148, 149]. Among local governments, Dobong-gu is establishing a comprehensive carbon-neutral city plan to protect 'climate-vulnerable' individuals [56, 57, 58, 79, 107, 114, 116, 133, 143], and the Yongin City Council is demonstrating leading efforts by launching 'Carbon Neutrality Research Institute IV' to commence research on circular economy policies [55, 66, 71, 74, 75, 83, 97, 100, 105, 125, 131]. In addition, various community participations and practices are continuing, such as the expansion of electric vehicle supply in Jincheon County [62, 80, 98, 126, 132, 136, 142], carbon neutrality point donations in Gimhae City [65, 69, 90, 99, 122], and contributions to carbon neutrality through the restoration of wildfire-damaged areas in Uiseong County [63, 72].

sections.title: ⚡ Renewable Energy Expansion and Challenges
sections.content: The expansion of renewable energy is a core pillar of climate change response, with various projects being pursued domestically and internationally. Korea Water Resources Corporation (K-water) is pursuing the development of a floating solar power facility with a maximum capacity of 90MW at Bustos Dam in the Philippines, seeking overseas expansion [25, 28, 44, 48], and Geurin Energy is accelerating its business by securing solar power generation permits totaling 379MW in the Jeonnam-Gwangju region [164, 182, 185, 188, 196, 206, 211, 214, 215, 217]. Siheung City expects to save over 20 million won annually in operating costs and achieve carbon neutrality by supplying customized renewable energy facilities to three public facilities [129, 146, 151, 155, 157, 166, 167, 168, 170, 173, 174, 177, 186, 194, 197, 201, 202, 205, 208, 209, 210, 213, 216], and Yesan County was selected for the new and renewable energy convergence project for 10 consecutive years, receiving an 'excellent' rating in the top 10% nationwide [154, 156, 160, 161, 162, 163, 171, 176, 187, 189, 193, 199, 204]. However, as pointed out by the statement 'No grid without ESS in the era of 100GW renewable energy,' discussions on stabilizing the power grid and expanding Energy Storage Systems (ESS) remain crucial challenges [153, 203], and concerns that artificial intelligence might increase fossil fuel use rather than aid renewable energy deployment, along with instances of some countries discarding solar power generation, illustrate the complex obstacles in the renewable energy transition process [158, 180, 181].

briefing.closing: Based on the severity of the climate crisis discussed in today's briefing and the domestic and international efforts to address it, we have once again confirmed the need for more proactive and integrated climate action. This concludes today's climate briefing.
